svg.text: Scaling scorecard — what holds, what breaks at millions of users
The shape is sound: static front end on a CDN · stateless edge functions · Postgres with RLS as the boundary. Nothing here needs a rewrite to scale.
the four blockers (#1–#4) are addressed — shared rate limiting · bounded-growth retention · indexed admin search · estimate-based counts.
The remaining items (#5–#8) are “plan for them”, not blockers. Ranked below, worst first. Written against the code as of this review.
Scales fine as-is — no change needed
GitHub Pages · static, cache-busted — millions of
readers is what a CDN is for
the boundary; correctness doesn’t degrade with
Semantic cache — match_cached_answer rides the HNSW index (~log-time) and offloads the LLM on common questions.
It gets MORE valuable at scale, not less.
Capacity ladder — how far each tier goes, and what unlocks the next
the demo’s volume is a rounding
only matters if reused for a
Order-of-magnitude, architecture-limited — not load-tested. Real concurrency ceilings depend on the Supabase plan (pooled connections, egress) and
Anthropic quotas (#8) — capacity planning with the providers, not a code change. The shape itself has no fixed ceiling; it scales with DB write capacity + quotas.
NEEDS ATTENTION — plan for them, not blockers
A per-warm-instance Map() meant ~no real limit at scale. Now a shared
fixed-window rate_hit() RPC (atomic upsert); fails over to the in-memory
counter if the DB blips, so an outage never blocks traffic.
Every turn / tool-call writes forever. Now prune_high_write(days)
enforces a retention window (nightly pg_cron). At web-scale: monthly
range partitions → retention becomes an instant drop.
Loaders fetched only the latest N with no filter — an old order or a
specific customer was unfindable. Now server-side date / email / keyword
count(exact) meant full scans on feedback / orders. Now date-bounded
counts stay exact & cheap; whole-table totals use count(estimated) from
the planner → O(1) regardless of size.
~3 sequential queries per chat (notes · last convo · orders), and the
tool loop adds more. Fix: collapse into one customer-bundle RPC, and
route PostgREST through the Supavisor pooler.
hold_serial / commission take FOR UPDATE on allocation_counter (id=1). A
non-issue for a 15,000-piece edition (scarcity is the point); switch to
a sequence / sharded counter only if reused for a high-volume product.
Goal scoring fired every signed-in turn. Now a substance gate + admin
goal_sample_rate (grade 1-in-N). The client-book note stays always-on
(per-customer product value, not analytics). Batch/queue if needed.
At millions of chats the binding limit is Anthropic token cost + per-
account limits, plus Supabase plan limits — not architecture. The
semantic cache is the main lever; the rest is capacity planning.
What this review closed now — admin filtering:
server-side filtering by date / email / keyword (incl. message content) + pagination, backed by btree + pg_trgm GIN indexes on every ILIKE column — so a match is found even if it’s the millionth row.
Source: SCALING.md. Status as of this review; re-check as the code changes. ✅ addressed · amber = partial / next step · slate = plan-for.
